title: 360p vs 720p vs 1080p Video Quality: Which Should You Choose?
description: What's the difference between 360p, 720p and 1080p video quality? Learn what resolution means, how it affects file size, and how to pick the right one.
body:
When you download a video, you're usually given a few choices like 360p, 720p and 1080p. So which one should you pick? This article explains the difference between 360p, 720p and 1080p video quality in plain language, so you can choose the resolution that fits your needs, your data plan and your phone's storage.

What do 360p, 720p and 1080p mean?

These numbers show the resolution, meaning the number of pixel lines along the short side of the video. The bigger the number, the more detail it can show. The letter “p” stands for progressive scan, a way of displaying images that's standard in digital video.

  • 360p: about 640 × 360 pixels for a horizontal video. It counts as low standard quality.
  • 720p: about 1280 × 720 pixels, often called HD.
  • 1080p: about 1920 × 1080 pixels, known as Full HD.

For vertical videos like the ones all over social media, the dimensions are flipped. For example, a vertical 1080p video is about 1080 × 1920 pixels.

The difference between 360p, 720p and 1080p in practice

360p: saves data and storage

This resolution produces the smallest files. The picture is still fairly clear on a small phone screen, but fine text and facial details can look a bit blurry. It's a good fit if you just want to keep a funny video for a quick watch, or when you're running low on mobile data.

720p: the balanced choice

For many people, 720p is the sweet spot. The picture is already sharp on a phone screen, while the file is still lighter than 1080p. It suits tutorials, recipes or videos you want to rewatch a few times.

1080p: the sharpest

When detail matters, for example scenery videos, tutorials with small text, or videos you want to watch on a tablet, laptop or TV, go for 1080p. The trade-off is a bigger file and a longer download.

File size and data usage

In general, the higher the resolution, the bigger the file. But the exact size also depends on the length, how much movement there is in the video, and how it was compressed. Two videos of the same length can have different sizes. So instead of guessing numbers, stick to this simple rule: if storage or data is limited, lower the resolution.

How to choose the quality when downloading

With I Need Save, picking a quality is easy:

  1. In the social media app, tap Share and then Copy link.
  2. Open ineedsave.com and paste the link into the box, or tap Paste.
  3. Press Download.
  4. Look through the video options that appear, then choose the resolution you want.

The options available depend on the original post. Some videos offer everything from 360p to 1080p, others only one or two qualities. If the button shows Preparing…, wait a moment; the video is being processed and the download will start automatically.

Choosing 1080p can't make a video that was blurry to begin with look sharp. The downloaded quality will never be better than the video the creator uploaded.

What about the HEVC and H.264 codecs?

Besides resolution, something else affects whether a video plays smoothly: the codec. Some TikTok videos use the HEVC (H.265) codec. It's efficient, but very old phones may not play it smoothly. H.264 options play on almost every device. So if a video stutters on an old phone, try downloading it again with another available option. The full guide is in our article on downloaded videos that won't play.

Only need the sound?

If all you need is the music or audio from a video, there's no need to download it in 1080p. Choose the Audio option, either original quality or a 192 kbps MP3 converted from the video. It's usually much smaller and plays right away in a music app. The steps are explained in our guide on how to convert social media videos to MP3.

Whatever quality you choose, use downloaded videos for personal use and respect creators' copyright. Ask for permission before reposting and give credit.

Frequently asked questions

Which quality is best?

For watching on a phone, 720p is usually enough. Choose 1080p if you want to watch on a big screen, and 360p if you want to save storage.

Why is there no 1080p option?

The quality options follow the original video. If the creator uploaded at a lower resolution, or the platform only offers certain qualities, the 1080p option won't appear.

Do 1080p videos take longer to download?

Usually yes, because the file is bigger. The speed also depends on your internet connection.
